source.title: Temporal Regularization Training: Unleashing the Potential of Spiking Neural Networks
source.authors: Boxuan Zhang; Zhen Xu; Kuan Tao

record.tranche_reason: Tests temporal regularization training in spiking neural networks on CIFAR and neuromorphic image datasets, a new model family and training method setting for the claim.
record.gate_note: Reports training and test loss curves plus classification accuracy. Training-loss values are largely figure-only; Table 3 reports classification accuracy, not training classification error. Plain-versus-residual depth, random-label memorization, initialization comparisons, above-stability learning rates, and batch-normalization comparisons are not tested. Cited results from prior work are not extracted.
record.test_reason: The study evaluates a temporal regularization method for spiking networks, reporting test accuracy, generalization and training-loss curves. It does not measure CIFAR training classification error or test any other claim version. It adopts threshold-dependent batch normalization, explicitly relying on its training benefits, without comparing training with and without normalization.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that TRT mitigates temporal gradient vanishing theoretically, improves generalization and reported accuracy empirically, and produces flatter local loss landscapes. They also observe temporal information concentration during TRT and use it to explain time-decaying regularization.
record.recipe_differences: Directly trained spiking neural networks with surrogate gradients; TRT adds a time-decaying regularizer and combines cross-entropy and mean-squared-error losses. Comparisons include standard direct training and TET.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset, simulation length, regularization ratio eta, decay rate delta, and regularization settings affect reported accuracy or learning curves.

fits_no_version.finding: TRT improves reported test accuracy over SDT across the listed datasets and simulation lengths.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Temporal regularization can improve generalization accuracy in directly trained spiking neural networks.

fits_no_version.finding: On DVS-CIFAR10, TRT with eta=0.001 has training loss approaching zero; TET's training loss drops early and then fluctuates.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The training objective affects loss trajectories and overfitting in surrogate-gradient-trained spiking networks.

fits_no_version.finding: The authors analyze temporal gradient vanishing and visualize differences in loss-landscape flatness under TRT, TET and SDT.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Temporal regularization can compensate for temporal gradient vanishing and alter loss-landscape geometry in spiking networks.

record.problems: The claim concerns training classification error, but the numerical tables report accuracy and the textual learning-curve description reports loss. Several learning-curve results are figure-only. The compared methods and conditions are not a direct test of the claim's random-initialization, capacity, or random-label assertions.
record.rows_left_out: Table 1 and Table 2 report additional accuracy comparisons against methods reported in prior literature, rather than separate results of the study's own intervention; excluded under the rule for cited prior results. Figure 1 reports accuracy comparisons with L2 and weight decay but does not give sufficient condition-specific per-method values in text. Figure 2 eta sweeps, Table 4 delta sweep, Figure 3 loss landscapes, Figure 4 learning curves, Figure 5 firing rates and Figure 6 Fisher-information plots are not separately extracted where they do not report training classification error; Figure-only outcomes also lack precise numeric values. Appendix B includes additional eta learning curves and test-loss and accuracy curves; these do not report training classification error.

untested.parts: Near-zero training classification error on CIFAR-10/100, random or corrupted labels, and dependence on capacity, stopping or regularization.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student optimization, spurious-minimum frequencies and the effect of extra student neurons.
Training-error degradation with depth and comparisons of plain networks with identity shortcuts or special initialization.
Activation-matched initialization, signal propagation across depth, initialization-dependent training speed and trainable depth.
Learning rates relative to stability thresholds, curvature dynamics, recovery and divergence.
Training speed and learning-rate tolerance with versus without batch normalization, including Fixup comparisons.

record.verdict_notes: No version-specific verdict is warranted. Near-zero neuromorphic training loss does not establish V1, temporal gradient compensation does not test initialization in V4, and loss-landscape flatness does not measure V2's spurious-minimum frequency.

versions.untested_parts: Does not report training classification error, CIFAR-10/100 results with corrupted or random labels, or comparisons of model size, early stopping, or regularized recipes leaving substantial training error. The learning curves concern DVS-CIFAR10 and N-Caltech101.
